_readme: Registry of macOS commands that route to SecurityAgent (admin-password dialog) or
otherwise require root. This is DATA, not code: add an entry to cover a new command,
never edit privileged_broker.py to special-case one.
Matching: a shell command is split into segments (pipes, &&, ;, newlines); each
segment's executable basename is matched against `executable`, then `argv_prefix`
must be a prefix of the remaining arguments. An entry with an empty `argv_prefix`
matches every invocation of that executable.  Longest argv_prefix wins.
confidence:  observed  = seen prompting on this machine, with evidence on file
documented = vendor/man page states root or admin is required
inferred   = behaviour follows from the command class; unverified here
mutating:    true  = changes host state. NEVER coalesced, NEVER cached, NEVER
inherits another task's authorization. One prompt per request.
false = read-only query. Eligible for single-flight coalescing within
ttl_seconds.
cacheable:   true  = the authorized RESULT may be persisted for ttl_seconds and
replayed to later identical requests.
false = waiters may join an IN-FLIGHT invocation, but nothing is kept
once it drains (set ttl_seconds to 0 as well).
negative_ttl_seconds: how long a denial / cancellation / timeout is remembered.
This is the anti-retry-storm control. A non-zero value is what stops an
agent from re-prompting 14 seconds after the user dismissed the dialog.
It never grants anything: a cached negative can only DENY.

entries.notes: Dumps the Background Task Management store (login items, launch agents/daemons). Requires root; macOS shows a SecurityAgent dialog naming only 'sfltool'. NOT in sfltool(1), which documents only `sfltool archive`. Read-only and slow-changing, so a 15-minute shared result is safe and removes almost all repeat prompts.
Writes a snapshot directory of the SharedFileList store. Documented in sfltool(1). Creates files, so it is mutating and never coalesces.
Catch-all for undocumented sfltool subcommands. Unknown effect is treated as mutating: it gets its own prompt and inherits nothing.

Any sudo invocation. Conservatively mutating: the broker does not attempt to classify the inner command. Note sudo has its OWN timestamp cache (sudoers timestamp_timeout) which is independent of this broker and is not managed here.
`sudo -n` tells sudo to fail rather than prompt. Still a privileged request worth attributing and recording, but it can never open a dialog, so it is excluded from prompt counts.
System Integrity Protection. `csrutil status` is unprivileged and is excluded below; everything else changes or asserts boot policy.
Unprivileged. Listed so the broker positively EXCLUDES it rather than matching the csrutil catch-all.
Reads the signed-system-volume state. Unprivileged; seen misclassified by the csrutil catch-all before this entry existed.
Gatekeeper policy changes (--master-disable, --add, --remove, --enable) require root.
Unprivileged read.
Unprivileged assessment of a bundle.
`spctl -a` is the short form of --assess and is unprivileged. Distinct from `spctl --add`, which requires root. Seen misclassified by the spctl catch-all before this entry existed.
Unprivileged read.
FileVault enable/disable/add-user require an authenticating admin.
systemsetup requires root even for many -get verbs.
Opens a file with authorization rights; the whole point is a SecurityAgent prompt.
nvram writes and deletes require root. `nvram -p` (print) is unprivileged and excluded below.
Unprivileged read.
Apple-silicon boot policy utility; requires an admin credential.
Kernel extension management. Some inspect verbs are unprivileged; treated conservatively as mutating until an entry proves otherwise.
System update installs require root.
Setting power management for all profiles requires root.

Local directory node mutations (-create/-delete/-append/-merge) require root. Reads (-read/-list) generally do not, but are not separated here; a read that is wrongly classified mutating costs one extra prompt, never a wrong grant.
The system launchd domain requires root. The gui/<uid> domain does not and is not matched.
See launchctl-system-domain.
Installing to -target / requires root.
Explicitly acquires an authorization right; prompts by design.
Enables or disables the root account.
Enabling Time Machine requires root.
Destructive. Included so it is attributed loudly, not so it is made easier.
See diskutil-erase.
